title_en: Entering the town and the changed word
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: They were told to enter this town (7:161 says to dwell in it) and to eat from it wherever they wished, in plenty.
They were told to enter the gate bowing down and to say hittah; God would forgive their wrong deeds, and He would increase the reward of those who do good.
Those who did wrong changed the word for another word than the one that had been said to them.
So God sent down on those who did wrong a rijz from the sky (7:162 says sent upon them), because of their disobedience (7:162 says because of their wrongdoing).

chapters.summary_md: They were told to enter a town, eat from it freely, enter the gate bowing down and say hittah [c1][c2]. Those who did wrong changed the word, and God sent a rijz from the sky on them [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md:
They were told to enter this town and to eat from it wherever they wished, in plenty [c1]. They were to enter the gate bowing down and to say hittah [c2]. God would forgive their wrong deeds, and He would increase the reward of those who do good [c2].

Those who did wrong changed the word for another word than the one that had been said to them [c3]. So God sent down on them a rijz from the sky, because of their disobedience [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passages give the instruction in a different order: 2:58 speaks of entering while 7:161 speaks of dwelling [c1]. 2:59 names the reason for the rijz as disobedience and 7:162 as wrongdoing [c4]. The word hittah and the word rijz are left untranslated here because the ayat do not explain them [c2][c4].
chapters.kids_md: They were told to go into a town, eat what they liked there, go in through the gate bowing down and say one special word [c1][c2]. Some of them changed the word, and God sent something from the sky upon those who did wrong [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage sets a plain instruction beside a plain act of changing it [c2][c3]. Another is that forgiveness is described as following the saying of the word and the bowing at the gate [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which town is meant, who is addressed, and when this happened; the ayat name neither the town nor the people.
- Not established: what hittah means or what the changed word was.
- Not established: what the rijz was; the Arabic word is read in more than one way and is left untranslated.
- The verses do not say whether every person among them changed the word; they speak of those who did wrong.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the town, the word and the rijz. None is used in this draft.
The meaning of hittah and of rijz is open; a scholar should decide how the page should word them.
Neither passage names the people; the inventory links both passages to the same event by matching wording.
